page: Amazon Web Services m9g.4xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the custom AWS Graviton processor family. Built on the ARM64 architecture, it features 16 dedicated physical cores and 16 vCPUs running at 3.3 GHz, utilizing the ARMv9 Neoverse-V3 microarchitecture. The CPU configuration includes 64 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and 48 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 64.0 GB of system memory, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of RAM per core. This instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor, does not include local storage, and features a baseline network bandwidth of 8 Gbps. There are no onboard GPUs.

Benchmark results indicate strong single-core and memory performance. The server achieves top-tier results in single-threaded gzip compression (36.42 GB/sec), single-threaded bzip3 decompression (17.14 GB/sec), and Geekbench single-core testing (2334.0). Its memory subsystem is highly efficient, scoring in the top tier for PassMark memory performance and delivering a read-only small-block memory bandwidth of 2282.43 GB/sec. Multi-threaded performance is also robust, with a Geekbench multi-core score of 19581.0 and a PassMark database operations score of 29240.13, both placing in the top 25%. For lightweight machine learning tasks, it demonstrates strong text generation speeds of 30.2 tokens/sec on medium (7B) models and 376.71 tokens/sec on small (135M) models.

From a resource density perspective, the m9g.4xlarge offers high qualitative cost efficiency by utilizing energy-efficient ARM64 cores that deliver high single-threaded performance without the overhead of simultaneous multithreading. However, workloads requiring local NVMe storage or specialized x86 instruction sets (such as AVX-512 or AMX) will face compatibility limitations, as these features are absent. Given its balanced compute-to-memory ratio and high memory bandwidth, this server is well-suited for general-purpose workloads, including database operations, static web serving, text processing, and lightweight LLM inference.
